postgres_requirements.rationale: The catalog probe cannot be proven against a mock. Its correctness is a question about what pg_catalog.to_regprocedure returns for a specific signature grapheme, and the only falsifiable answer comes from a real PostgreSQL catalog holding first the seven-argument completion verb and then the nine-argument one. A disposable container is required to install both shapes in sequence and observe the probe inverting. Always via pnpm db:audit:disposable against a fresh throwaway container, destroyed afterwards; never staging, never production, never the canonical local Supabase stack. Both manifest paths are UNKNOWN because they are pre-implementation commitments, and because the nine-argument signature does not exist in any artifact at the base this manifest was frozen against — see the authority's finding F-RC-5.

positive_controls.description: Type and exhaustiveness. The execution result type and the interaction payload carry riskLevel and riskFlags as REQUIRED-and-nullable, not optional. Every one of the six interaction categories states a position: validator, proxy_reviewer, evidence_reviewer and audit_assistant derive values; advisor and composer supply explicit nulls. Adding a seventh category without stating its risk disposition must fail to compile. Catches MUT-RC-11, which typechecks under an optional field and is therefore invisible to the compiler alone.

Risk payload propagation. Both riskLevel AND riskFlags travel from the validator and reviewer results, through the governed execution result, into the interaction payload, and reach the completion call as arguments 8 and 9 in NEW_DB. Asserted per-field and not as a single object identity, so that dropping one field while keeping the other is caught. Catches MUT-RC-05.

Same-transaction persistence with Stage-A. In NEW_DB the risk values are filed on the stella_interactions row inside the SAME transaction that charges the quota — never a second statement, never a follow-up UPDATE. Also pins the fail-closed reconciliation: a NEW_DB completion that fails to persist risk returns a rejected outcome and the governed operation withholds the answer. FUTURE-DEPENDENT: the NEW_DB half cannot execute until stella_0017b exists and is installed in a disposable container. Declared explicitly as future-dependent rather than written as a silently-skipped test.

Idempotent replay. A replayed delivery is charged once and the ledger row is NOT overwritten with the second delivery's payload, in BOTH database states. Specifically: a replay must not overwrite a previously-filed risk_level with a null from a later delivery. The (organization_id, idempotency_key) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING contract is unchanged by the bridge. FUTURE-DEPENDENT for the NEW_DB half.

Rollback and probe inversion. After the nine-argument signature is dropped and the seven-argument form restored, the probe — once invalidated — returns OLD_DB and completion succeeds through seven arguments with no redeploy and no configuration change. Proves ROLLBACK_CONTRACT R-1, and proves it is the catalog and not a cached constant that drives the return. FUTURE-DEPENDENT: requires a disposable container in which both shapes can be installed and reverted.

Observable signature-mismatch reason. A refusal caused by the connected database not matching the arity the bridge expects is distinguishable, in the wrapper's own refusal reason, from an ordinary unavailability. Proves the authority's CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT.observability rule, without which the deployment contract is unenforceable in practice because its most likely violation presents as generic noise.

negative_controls.description: Old/new signature mismatch negatives. A seven-argument call issued against a database holding only the nine-argument form is REFUSED, and a nine-argument call issued against a database holding only the seven-argument form is REFUSED. Neither silently succeeds, neither silently degrades, and neither is retried into the other arity within the same transaction. Together with N-RC-01 and N-RC-02 this is what makes the bridge falsifiable in both directions.

Deployment-order guard. The prohibited cell D-3 — an old runtime without the bridge against a new nine-argument database — is REFUSED and is observably attributed to a signature mismatch rather than to unavailability. Proves the deployment contract has a detectable violation rather than only a documented one. Catches MUT-RC-09 in its deployment aspect.

No audit-log source-of-truth fallback. No code path reads a risk level from audit_logs, and a successful audit_logs write does not satisfy any risk-persistence obligation. Asserted as an absence over the slice's surface, not as a single call-site check, because the defect this forbids is a plausible shortcut that would appear to close the gap. The existing best-effort audit write must still be present — the control proves it is not the SOURCE OF TRUTH, not that it was deleted. Catches MUT-RC-06.
Removing the seven-argument branch is CAUGHT. A bridge that can only call nine arguments fails against an un-applied database. Catches MUT-RC-02.

Removing the nine-argument branch is CAUGHT. A bridge that can only call seven arguments never feeds Stage-A's parameters, silently restoring the original defect while appearing to succeed. Catches MUT-RC-03.

The prohibited fallback shape is CAUGHT, and is caught EXHIBITING SQLSTATE 25P02 in_failed_sql_transaction. A mutant that issues the nine-argument call first and attempts a seven-argument fallback after it fails, inside the same transaction, must be observed producing 25P02 — not merely observed being slower or returning a generic rejection. A control that only asserts 'the fallback did not succeed' is vacuous here, because the fallback cannot succeed for reasons unrelated to the guarantee being tested. Catches MUT-RC-04 and proves CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT P-1.

No manual flag. The arity is not selectable by any environment variable, configuration value or build flag. Asserted as an absence over the slice's surface: a mutant that introduces a flag and reads it to choose the branch is CAUGHT even if the flag's default preserves correct behavior — the defect is the existence of a second source of truth, not a wrong value. Catches MUT-RC-01 and proves RC-06.

FIBIU-19 disjointness. The slice's diff touches no path in FIBIU-19's write surface — lib/pipeline/sroi-calculation.ts, lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts, app/app/projects/[projectId]/pipeline/calculation/**, db/migrations/**. lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts is the sharpest case because it is chokepoint SW-6, the domain authority's own stated reason for serializing FIBIU-19 before FIBIU-20. Re-derived against the implementing lane's own base, never inherited from this manifest, because FIBIU-19's surface can grow. Catches MUT-RC-07 and is the mechanical condition on which the owner's sequencing exception depends.

No premature apply. Nothing in the slice applies, schedules, triggers or authorizes an application of stella_0017b to any database that is not a disposable throwaway container. No artifact claims the FIBDB-053 external G2 gate is resolved. Additionally: the bridge is not readable as permission for validator or reviewer to be production-ready against an un-applied database. Catches MUT-RC-09.

Advisor readiness edge is untouched. The slice's edit to app/actions/stella/advisor.ts is confined to the explicit-null risk fields. The import of getSroiCalculationReadiness from lib/pipeline/sroi-calculation.ts and its call site are not modified, re-typed, re-ordered, wrapped or re-scoped. This is the single read edge between the slice and FIBIU-19; the constraint keeps a sequencing exception granted on disjointness from being spent on an incidental refactor.

No protected path. The slice's diff contains no path matching ods-scope's DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS — db/prepared/**, db/migrations/**, db/baseline/**, docs/ops/fib/**, docs/ops/pc01b/**, docs/ops/im01b/**, docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json — and no non-canonically-cased variant of one. db/prepared/** is the likeliest violation because the Stage-A SQL lives there and merging the two nodes would look like convenience. Catches MUT-RC-08 and sustains NEW_ODS_REQUIRED=NO.

Stage-A reference reconciliation. Before final implementation, the nine-argument signature this slice probes for is reconciled against the INTEGRATED Stage-A authority — argument names, types and order — and a divergence STOPS the lane rather than being silently absorbed. Guards the runtime-first hazard that the probe is written against a contract whose counterpart does not yet exist.

Probe grapheme. The probe literal uses the to_regprocedure INPUT grapheme, not the pg_catalog grapheme (bpchar/varchar/int4/_text) and not the SQL declaration grapheme. A probe in the wrong grapheme returns NULL forever, pinning the bridge to OLD_DB on a database that is already NEW_DB — filing no risk while reporting success. This mutant FAILS SILENT, so a control asserting only 'the bridge works' passes it; the control must assert the probe returns TRUE against a real catalog holding the nine-argument function. Catches MUT-RC-12.

mutation_controls.description: Replace the catalog probe with a manual environment flag or configuration value selecting the arity. Must be caught by N-RC-04.
Remove the seven-argument branch, leaving only the nine-argument call. Must be caught by T2 and N-RC-01.
Remove the nine-argument branch, leaving only the seven-argument call. Must be caught by T2 and N-RC-02.
Issue the nine-argument call first and fall back to seven arguments after it fails, inside the same transaction. Must be caught by N-RC-03, exhibiting 25P02.
Omit riskFlags from the propagation chain while keeping riskLevel. Must be caught by T3, whose assertions are per-field for exactly this reason.
Source the risk value from audit_logs instead of from the validator or reviewer result. Must be caught by T8.
Touch a FIBIU-19 path, lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts being the sharpest case. Must be caught by N-RC-05.
Add a protected path, db/prepared/** being the likeliest, to the slice's diff. Must be caught by N-RC-08 and by the ods_scope exit gate.
Allow Stage-A apply before the companion is integrated and deployed. Must be caught by T6 and N-RC-06.
Roll the runtime back before the SQL rollback, manufacturing the prohibited old-runtime-against-new-database cell. Must be caught by T7.
Make riskLevel or riskFlags optional on the execution result type instead of required-and-nullable. The mutant typechecks, so the compiler alone does not catch it. Must be caught by T1.
Write the probe literal in the pg_catalog grapheme instead of the to_regprocedure input grapheme. Fails silent. Must be caught by N-RC-10.
